A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and complete, including v1 Appendices A–E and v2 Appendices A–G. The retained vector diffusion construction, theorems, and ellipsoid experiments establish continuity despite the changed title and expanded scope.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original ellipsoid diameter and node-level vector prediction experiments in Tables 1–2, with runtime results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains the ellipsoid results and adds original wind reconstruction and neural representation experiments in Sections 4.2–4.3, Tables 3–4, and Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The original ellipsoid architecture is retained under the VDW-GNN name. However, Appendix F adds a vector-only wind model with neighbor-feature concatenation and residual prediction, while Appendix G adds a neural embedding model with supervised contrastive learning, hard-negative sampling, and neighbor-based inference for unseen nodes. These are substantive procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic ellipsoid tasks, v2 evaluates reconstruction of real-world wind measurements and representation learning from 24-channel macaque neural recordings across 44 experimental days. These introduce new domains, task requirements, and masked-sensor and unseen-trial scenarios.

E2.justification: The ellipsoid comparator set is unchanged after matching ESc-GNN to VDW-GNN. The new wind comparison evaluates DD-TNN alongside retained baseline families, and the neural experiment introduces evaluated comparisons with MARBLE, CEBRA, and LFADS (Tables 3–4).

E3.justification: The ellipsoid splits and training recipe are retained. New protocols include 2,000 wind measurements with observed/masked partitions, directed observed-to-masked graph connections, and random rotation testing. Neural evaluation introduces whole-trial holdouts, per-day cross-validation, three-dimensional embeddings, SVM probing, and neighbor-based test embedding estimation (Appendices F–G). These are new experiments, not revisions of an earlier neural or wind protocol.

E4.justification: v2 extends rotation robustness testing to wind reconstruction using randomly sampled rotations between 90 and 160 degrees (Section 4.2 and Table 3). The original ellipsoid non-equivariant ablation and rotation tests remain unchanged, making this a limited extension of the existing robustness analysis.

E5.justification: The existing ellipsoid mean-and-standard-deviation reporting across five folds is retained. v2 additionally specifies five wind repetitions with distinct sampling and rotation seeds, defines aggregation across daily neural cross-validation means, and adds two-sided paired Wilcoxon tests in Figure 5. These supplement the previous descriptive uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in ellipsoid Tables 1–2 are unchanged. New results include wind MSE of 2.7546 ± 0.3671 and rotated MSE of 3.2266 ± 0.5255, plus neural classification accuracy of 0.66 ± 0.14 versus MARBLE’s 0.65 ± 0.12, without a significant difference. New runtime and parameter results are added, while the ellipsoid inference-time entries from v1 Tables 3–4 are removed.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 adds an explicit optional manifold setting with intrinsic dimension d < D, tangent-bundle-valued features, and connection-Laplacian heat-flow notation. The main frame and equivariance theorems and their proofs are retained. Non-dyadic applicability already had a counterpart in v1 Appendix D, so its expanded discussion does not establish a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion shift from presenting a particular equivariant scattering GNN with parameter-efficient performance to presenting vector diffusion wavelets as the basis of a broader GNN family. v2 explicitly claims effectiveness on wind and neural data and elevates the existing frame properties into the principal contribution statement.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations connecting vector diffusion to connection-Laplacian heat flow, wind masking to sensor failures, and whole-trial holdouts to generalization without neighborhood leakage. It also qualifies the wind training-time advantage with approximately 1.1 seconds of preprocessing and explicitly acknowledges the nonsignificant accuracy difference from MARBLE. v1’s empirical interpretation was largely confined to rotation sensitivity and parameter efficiency.

D1.justification: Appendices F–G disclose wind coordinate conversion, graph and model configurations, neural preprocessing, contrastive sampling, SVM settings, and optimization procedures. The disclosed code repository changes from esc-gnn to vdw-gnns, and CUDA 12.4 is specified. A new inconsistency remains: Appendix D says all runs use one GPU, while Appendix E.5 retains the four-GPU TFN exception; this does not establish an actual hardware change.

R1.justification: The new manifold-hypothesis discussion substantially expands positioning within manifold learning and tangent-bundle neural networks, including Battiloro et al. and foundational diffusion-map work. Sections 4.3 and Appendix G further position the method relative to MARBLE, CEBRA, and LFADS. This extends the earlier emphasis on scattering and equivariant GNNs.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, renames ESc-GNN, and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and background. The standalone message-passing background is consolidated, a manifold-hypothesis subsection is introduced, and the architecture and complexity appendices are reorganized. The experiments are structured into three application subsections.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. v2 adds a local-frame illustration, redraws and moves the architecture diagram into the main text, and adds wind/neural result tables and a daily-accuracy plot. The original equivariance illustrations remain as Figures 3–4. Ellipsoid runtime tables are reformatted without their inference-time columns.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1’s synthetic-only empirical support through documented wind and neural evaluations, relevant baselines, held-out-trial testing, and paired significance analysis (Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendices F–G). These strengthen evidence of practical applicability while appropriately qualifying the MARBLE comparison. Removed inference timings, conflicting GPU statements, and differing supervision across neural baselines limit specific comparisons, but the overall evidential gain remains substantial.
